'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Yemeni Civil War (2014–present)|Yemeni Civil War]]
**[[Ma'rib Campaign]]
***[[Houthi]] forces take control of the [[Marib Dam]], al-Balaq, Dahwan, and Athaf mountains, and the Kholan area, among others, as coalition forces retreat. This is the first time since 2015 that the Houthis control Marib Dam, which gives the Houthis fire control of the southern road to Marib. [https://english.iswnews.com/17525/marib-dam-was-liberated-isis-and-al-qaeda-still-could-not-stop-ansarallah/ (ISWNews)]
*[[Insurgency in the Maghreb (2002–present)|Insurgency in the Maghreb]], [[Mali War]]
**[[Jihadism|Jihadist]] [[insurgent]]s kill nine people in an [[ambush]] in [[Burkina Faso]], while another jihadist attack near [[Bandiagara]], [[Mopti Region]], [[Mali]], kills nine people and leaves others missing, according to local [[government of Mali|government]] officials. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-burkina-security/at-least-18-killed-in-attacks-in-burkina-faso-and-mali-idUSKBN2AI2PL?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[ISIL insurgency in Iraq (2017–present)|ISIL insurgency in Iraq]]
**[[Secretary General of NATO]] [[Jens Stoltenberg]] announces an increase in [[NATO]] personnel in [[Iraq]] from 500 to around 4,000 amid a surge in [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant|ISIL]] activity in the country. The training mission will also be expanded to more areas beyond [[Baghdad]] and include more Iraqi security institutions, according to Stoltenberg. [https://www.france24.com/en/europe/20210218-nato-to-expand-iraq-mission-to-around-4-000-personnel (France 24)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[News Media Bargaining Code]]
**[[Facebook]] bans [[Australia]]n news publishers from posting and Australian users from viewing and sharing news content in a preemptive retaliation move against the [[Australian Competition & Consumer Commission]]'s (ACCC) proposed News Media Bargaining Code, which would require Facebook to pay to host Australian news content. A number of key [[government of Australia|government]] and charity organisations were also blocked for several hours. [https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2021/feb/18/facebook-blocks-health-departments-charities-and-its-own-pages-in-botched-australia-news-ban (''The Guardian'')]
**[[Alphabet Inc.]] agrees to begin paying [[News Corp]] for news content. News Corp [[CEO]] [[Robert Thomson (executive)|Robert Thomson]] credits the ACCC's proposed legislation with making the deal possible. [https://www.nytimes.com/2021/02/17/technology/facebook-google-australia-news.html (''The New York Times'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2020–21 North American winter]]
**[[February 13–17, 2021 North American winter storm]], [[2021 Texas power crisis]]
***In [[Texas]], power is restored to millions of homes, but millions of people lack safe drinking water and 325,000 homes and businesses remain without power. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-usa-weather-idINKBN2AI151 (Reuters)]
 
'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Oceania]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]]
****[[COVID-19 lockdowns|Lockdown restrictions]] are eased in [[Victoria (Australia)|Victoria]] as contact tracers are confident that all cases linked to a recent outbreak are [[self-isolating]]. People are permitted to leave their homes for non-essential reasons but are required to wear a [[Face masks during the COVID-19 pandemic|mask]] when they are indoors. Private gatherings of up to five people and public gatherings of up to 20 people are once again permitted. Non-essential businesses and on-campus learning have been reopened, and businesses that were working from home can have up to 50% of their employees return to the office. [https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2021/feb/17/victorias-lockdown-to-lift-at-midnight-but-some-restrictions-remain-in-place (''The Guardian'')]
****[[South Australia]] reopens its land border with Victoria to the state's regional population, while still restricting travelers from [[Melbourne]], the location of the recent outbreak. Similar restrictions are also in place at the [[New South Wales]] and [[Tasmania]]n borders. [https://www.9news.com.au/national/coronavirus-update-border-restrictions-lifted-with-regional-victoria/6c6a67d3-2e3c-406f-964c-e4e51c9a0ec3 (9 News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in New Zealand]]
****Restrictions are eased in [[New Zealand]], with [[Auckland]] downgraded to alert level 2 and the rest of the country to alert level 1. Most Auckland schools are reopened and masks are made mandatory on public transportation. [https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/politics/covid-19-coronavirus-auckland-to-level-2-rest-of-nz-to-level-1-despite-another-new-covid-case/N6OMWI6DLL4NLJGZ6AN7I2AHTU/ (''New Zealand Herald'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Hong Kong]]
****[[Hong Kong]] grants [[emergency use authorization]] to the [[Sinovac]] [[CoronaVac]] [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]], making it the second vaccine to be approved in the city. [https://qz.com/1974171/hong-kong-just-approved-chinas-sinovac-covid-19-vaccine/amp/ (Quartz)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia]]
****[[Malaysia]] reports a record 25 deaths in the past 24 hours, thereby surpassing 1,000 deaths from [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]]. [https://www.thestar.com.my/news/nation/2021/02/18/covid-19-2712-new-cases-highest-daily-deaths-of-25-bring-total-fatalities-to-1030 (''The Star'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Nepal]]
****[[Nepal]] approves the emergency use of the [[Sinopharm]] [[vaccine]], which is the second vaccine to be approved in the country. [https://www.deccanherald.com/international/world-news-politics/nepal-approves-chinas-sinopharm-covid-19-vaccine-to-purchase-astrazeneca-shots-from-india-952564.html (''Deccan Herald'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Saudi Arabia]]
****[[Saudi Arabia]]'s Food and Drug Authority approves the use of the [[Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine|Oxford–AstraZeneca]] [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]]. [https://gulfnews.com/world/gulf/saudi/covid-19-saudi-arabia-approves-oxford-astrazeneca-vaccine-1.77287875 (''Gulf News'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Africa]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Nigeria]]
****[[Nigeria]] approves the emergency use of the [[Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine|Oxford–AstraZeneca]] vaccine produced by the [[Serum Institute of India]]. [https://www.bloomberg.com/amp/news/articles/2021-02-18/nigeria-approves-astrazeneca-vaccines-for-emergency-use (Bloomberg)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Zimbabwe]]
****[[Zimbabwe]] begins its vaccination programme against [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]] using China's [[Sinopharm]] vaccine. Health minister and [[Vice President of Zimbabwe|Vice President]] [[Constantino Chiwenga]] is the first person to receive the vaccine. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/africa/zimbabwe-begins-covid-19-vaccination-with-chinese-jabs/2149125 (Anadolu Agency)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in South America]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil]]
****[[Brazil]] surpasses 10 million cases of COVID-19, being the second country to do so after the [[United States]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/health-coronavirus-brazil/amid-new-strain-stalling-vaccinations-brazil-passes-10-million-covid-19-cases-idUSL8N2KO7WJ (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Venezuela]]
****[[Venezuela]] launches a vaccination program against COVID-19 using [[Sputnik V COVID-19 vaccine|Sputnik V]] vaccine starting with frontline health workers. [https://www.voanews.com/covid-19-pandemic/venezuela-launches-covid-19-vaccination-program (VOA)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Nevada]], [[501.V2 variant]]
****[[Nevada]] reports their first case of the 501.V2 variant in a person who travelled from [[South Africa]] to [[Reno, Nevada|Reno]] and who later began showing symptoms of COVID-19. [https://www.usnews.com/news/best-states/nevada/articles/2021-02-18/nevada-reports-1st-case-of-virus-variant-from-south-africa (U.S. News and World Report)]
**[[COVID-19 vaccine]], [[501.V2 variant]]
***Lab studies suggest that the [[Pfizer–BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine|Pfizer–BioNTech]] and [[Moderna COVID-19 vaccine]]s are significantly less effective in providing antibody protection against the 501.V2 variant of the disease, which is most prevalent in [[South Africa]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2021/feb/18/south-african-covid-variant-may-cut-pfizer-vaccine-protection-by-two-thirds (''The Guardian'')]

'''International relations'''
*[[Iran–United States relations]], [[United States sanctions against Iran]]
**The [[Presidency of Joe Biden|Biden administration]] rescinds the [[United Nations|UN]] sanctions placed on [[Iran]] by his predecessor [[Donald Trump]], seen as a potential step towards rejoining the [[Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action]]. The "snapback" of sanctions had been ignored by the rest of the world. [https://apnews.com/article/joe-biden-donald-trump-iran-united-states-united-nations-aa8f38fa3bf7de3c09a469ec91664a3c (AP)]
*[[Israel–Syria relations]]
**[[Israel]] and [[Syria]] carry out a [[Russia]]n-mediated [[prisoner exchange]]. An Israeli woman who crossed the [[Borders of Israel|border]] into Syria's [[Quneitra Governorate]] and was detained by the [[Syrian Armed Forces|Syrian military]], is returned in exchange for two Syrian shepherds held by the [[Israel Defense Forces]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-middle-east-56100740 (BBC News)]
*[[2021 Myanmar coup d'état]]
**[[Canada]] and the [[United Kingdom]] announce sanctions on the [[State Administration Council|military junta]] generals in response to the coup and the arbitrary detention of [[Aung San Suu Kyi]] and other political figures. [https://www.france24.com/en/asia-pacific/20210218-uk-canada-sanction-myanmar-generals-after-coup (France 24)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2020–2021 Indian farmers' protest]], [[Internet Censorship in India]]
**A [[Government of India|New Delhi]] court sends climate activist [[Disha Ravi]] to jail for allegedly sharing a "toolkit" on [[social media]] in connection with the ongoing farmers' protest against [[2020 Indian agriculture acts|three farm bills]] as it investigates further. Ms. Ravi, a resident of [[Bangalore]], was arrested on February 4 and flown overnight to New Delhi. [https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/toolkit-case-delhi-court-sends-disha-ravi-to-3-day-judicial-custody/article33880941.ece (''The Hindu'')]
*[[Kyrgyzstan]]'s [[State Committee for National Security (Kyrgyzstan)|State Committee for National Security]] rearrests former deputy chief of Custom Service [[Raimbek Matraimov]] due to an ongoing investigation into allegations of money laundering. The arrest comes days after hundreds protested in the capital of [[Bishkek]] over a court commuting his sentence last week. [https://www.rferl.org/a/kyrgyzstan-powerbroker-matraimov-rearrested-protests-corruption/31109843.html (''Radio Free Europe'')]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Prime Minister of Georgia|Georgian Prime Minister]] [[Giorgi Gakharia]] resigns due to disagreements with his cabinet over the detention of prominent opposition figure [[Nika Melia]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-georgia-politics-minister/georgias-prime-minister-resigns-opposition-calls-for-early-election-idUSKBN2AI0X5?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[President of Algeria|Algerian President]] [[Abdelmadjid Tebboune]], in a televised address, announces he will pardon dozens of protestors associated with the [[2019–20 Algerian protests|Hirak movement]], reshuffle the [[Cabinet of Algeria|cabinet]] within 48 hours and will dissolve the [[People's National Assembly|lower chamber]] of parliament to make way for [[2021 Algerian legislative election|new elections]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/2/18/algeria-calls-early-legislative-elections (Al Jazeera)]

'''Science and technology'''
*[[Mars 2020]]
**The rover ''[[Perseverance (rover)|Perseverance]]'' successfully lands on [[Mars]] as part of the [[Mars 2020]] mission. [https://www.nytimes.com/live/2021/02/18/science/nasa-mars-landing (''The New York Times'')]
*A coalition of technology companies including Facebook, [[Google]], and [[Amazon (company)|Amazon]], as well as the [[United States Chamber of Commerce]], file a federal lawsuit against the U.S. state of [[Maryland]] for passing a [[Gross receipts tax|gross revenue tax]] on [[Online advertising|digital ads]] by non-media companies. It is the first tax of its kind in the nation. [https://www.theverge.com/2021/2/18/22289825/maryland-digital-services-tax-lawsuit-internet-association (''The Verge'')]
